analysis.title: Year Ahead 2027: Sustaining resilience (Asia Pacific edition, UBS House View)
key_insights: UBS CIO base case for 2027 is solid earnings, continued AI investment, easing inflation and a more balanced risk-reward for global equities. It advises staying invested, cutting excess concentration, and diversifying through fixed income, commodities, currencies and alternatives.

Global equities moved to Neutral, along with US equities and Asia ex-Japan/EM equities. The reasons given are high expectations, index concentration (top 10 are about 40% of the S&P 500), and AI capex exposure. Eurozone is the preferred region, with 15% EPS growth matching the US from lower valuations.

Global AI investment is forecast to rise from USD 1.0tr in 2026 to USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028, versus consensus of USD 1.6tr and USD 1.8tr. About 80% of 2027 spend comes from Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and SpaceX.

Support for AI demand: USD 2.5tr of contracted cloud orders not yet recognized as revenue (about 6x trailing 12-month cloud revenue), hyperscaler cloud revenue +57% y/y in 3Q26 (fourth straight quarter of acceleration), and GPU pricing above its level at the January 2025 DeepSeek launch. Token costs have more than halved since May while usage rose sixfold.

AI risks: capacity outrunning demand, slower AI lab revenue growth, weaker cloud utilization, circular financing, rising neocloud borrowing costs, and power and permitting constraints. The 2028 pipeline is less certain than 2027.

Inflation is expected to moderate, with 2027 average forecasts of 2.3% US, 3.1% Eurozone and 3.4% global (2026: 3.4%, 3.1%, 3.8%). Rates stay structurally higher than in the 2010s because of AI, defense and energy investment and heavy sovereign issuance. Several central banks may still hike in late 2026 or early 2027.

Fixed income is rated Attractive, with intermediate duration (2-10 years) preferred. UBS favors quality bonds, EM bonds (EMBI about 7.1%, CEMBI about 7.0%) and US high yield (about 8.3%), and limits maturities beyond 10 years because of fiscal and term-premium risk.

Government debt: UBS expects fiscal strain but no broad sovereign crisis. Long-dated yields are at multi-decade highs while credit risk premiums are subdued. It would become concerned on difficult bond auctions, weak policy credibility, or spillover to banks.

Geopolitics: the Strait of Hormuz closure pushed oil up 52% year to date. UBS expects the Middle East and Ukraine wars to continue and US-China tech competition to persist, producing volatility without displacing economics as the main driver. The S&P 500 has recovered from the average geopolitical shock in 16 days.

Asia: regional earnings are expected to grow 20% in 2027, the highest of any major region. MSCI Asia ex-Japan returned more than 80% over three years, and Asia IT returned almost three times the regional index. UBS expects another strong year for AI supply chains in 2027 but a much less certain 2028, with memory prices possibly falling from mid-2027.

Asia positioning: favor Taiwanese foundries, quality semiconductors and hardware, and Asian financials (China, Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong banks). Also favor China health care, India, Japan domestic and defense, and ASEAN data-center power suppliers. Limit memory to a mid-single-digit share of tech exposure and trim small/mid-cap hardware.

Asian credit and FX: Asia IG yields about 5.8% and HY about 8.0%, with carry preferred over duration. UBS favors CNY, SGD and TWD, sees weaker balance-of-payments dynamics constraining IDR, INR and PHP, and expects USDJPY range-bound. Overall FX upside is 2-3%.

Gold is a long-term holding with a December 2027 target of USD 5,000/oz. UBS suggests adding on pullbacks below USD 4,000/oz and warns gold could trade below that near term on high real yields and a firm dollar. Copper is the preferred industrial metal, at USD 15,500/tonne by end-2027.

Currencies: GBP is the preferred G10 carry currency (4.0% policy rate, another hike expected early 2027). UBS also favors diversified EM carry (MXN, ZAR, BRL, INR) and sees CHF as a funding currency that underperforms on total return. The US dollar outlook is balanced.

Volatility and structured strategies: index-level implied volatility is subdued while single-stock volatility is high. UBS favors capital preservation structures, structured yield (conditional coupons, with barrier-breach risk) and predefined-entry strategies.

Alternatives: favor low-net and market-neutral hedge funds, merger arbitrage, operationally focused middle-market private equity, secondaries (volumes up about 15% y/y in 1H), and core/core-plus infrastructure. Private debt is Neutral.

Scenario probabilities and December 2027 targets are given in the Key data points and Tension points fields. The base case (50%) puts the S&P 500 at 8,200, the Goldilocks case (20%) at 9,500, the yield reset (10%) at 7,000 and the AI bust (20%) at 5,500.

sector_views.rationale: Automation, defense, transport infrastructure, power networks and electrification support earnings. UBS prefers diversified end-market exposure over data-center-dependent names.
Medical innovation, obesity treatments and diagnostics support revenue, and earnings are less tied to corporate investment.

Keep AI exposure but focus on quality: financially strong hyperscalers, plus leaders in compute, foundry and semiconductor equipment. Stay cautious on lower-quality suppliers, leveraged capacity providers and bottleneck beneficiaries reliant on price increases.
Banks in China, Japan, Singapore and Hong Kong offer defensive growth and income, attractive dividends and capital returns, and less dependence on AI capex.
Aging population, innovation, commercialization and recovering biotech funding support earnings diversification.
Offers exposure to wider AI adoption with less dependence on data center construction.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 earnings are on track to rise 29% in 2026 (UBS CIO estimate), with a further 15% forecast for 2027.
Eurozone EPS growth is forecast at 15% for 2027, matching the US.
MSCI Asia ex-Japan EPS growth is forecast at 20% for 2027, the highest among major regions.
The median private buyout company delivered 7% revenue growth and 9% EBITDA growth in the second quarter (reported figures cited in the report).

macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS expects US inflation to fall from 3.4% in 2026 as energy effects fade.
Down from 5.9% in March 2022, which reduces the risk of a wage-price spiral.
The report says global growth is on track for 3.3% in 2026. Its forecast table shows 3.5% for 2027.
From the UBS forecast table, versus 2.4% in 2026.
The report's own text says some central banks, and by implication the Fed, may tighten further. The table shows a 50bp rise from spot.
UBS expects a modest decline later in 2027, with yields staying above pre-pandemic norms.
Oil is up 52% year to date because of the Hormuz closure, and UBS expects it to ease.
Unchanged from 2026 in the UBS forecast table.

trade_ideas.description: Add gold on pullbacks below USD 4,000/oz as a long-term allocation
trade_ideas.rationale: Central bank buying, resilient ETF holdings, and fiscal concerns provide structural support around that level.
trade_ideas.risk: High US real yields and a firm dollar could push gold below USD 4,000/oz in the short run.

trade_ideas.description: Build copper exposure during periods of weakness, targeting USD 15,500/tonne by end-2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Grid, data center and AI infrastructure demand meets slow supply response.
trade_ideas.risk: Sensitivity to Chinese activity, inventories, trade policy and substitution can cause sizeable corrections.

trade_ideas.description: Long GBP carry, funded with CHF and diversified EM carry (MXN, ZAR, BRL, INR)
trade_ideas.rationale: UK policy rate of 4.0% with another hike expected gives a yield advantage over EUR, CHF and JPY, and low currency volatility supports carry.
trade_ideas.risk: UK fiscal credibility, and a risk-off move reviving safe-haven demand for CHF.

trade_ideas.description: Long CNY, SGD and TWD against weaker-balance-of-payments Asian currencies (IDR, INR, PHP)
trade_ideas.rationale: Stronger external balances and policy support favor CNY, SGD and TWD.
trade_ideas.risk: Persistently high oil, a stronger dollar or a disorderly refinancing cycle.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Taiwanese foundries within Asian AI picks and shovels
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong growth outlook and relatively low oversupply risk.
trade_ideas.risk: A sharp break in the AI investment cycle or capex cuts in 2028.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Eurozone equities versus the US
trade_ideas.rationale: Comparable 15% EPS growth from lower valuations, with less reliance on a few AI-linked companies.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker global growth or a European energy shock.

risk_factors: AI capex fails to deliver returns, or capacity growth outstrips demand (AI bust scenario).
Persistent inflation forces further central bank hikes and resets bond yields higher.
Debt refinancing at higher yields, difficult auctions, or weaker policy credibility.
Sustained disruption to Middle East shipping or Gulf infrastructure, or loss of energy supplies from the Ukraine war.
Escalating US-China export controls or trade restrictions.
Stronger dollar and high oil prices pressuring Asian economies with weak external balances.
Concentration of index earnings in a handful of mega-cap companies.
AI financing complexity, neocloud borrowing costs, and power and permitting constraints.
Asian memory oversupply, with prices potentially declining from mid-2027.
charts_described: Figure 1 plots yearly hyperscaler capex growth against consensus estimates from the start of each year, and the report states that actual capex consistently exceeded estimates.
Asian credit yield chart as of 12 November 2026: Europe IG 4.2%, Asia IG 5.8%, AT1 CoCo 6.8%, Asia HY 8.0%, US HY 8.4%.
MSCI Asia ex-Japan 2027 EPS revisions chart, indexed to 100 in June 2025: about 170 by October 2026 including TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix, and about 140 excluding them.
China grid investment chart: forecast to reach around CNY 1.3trn by 2030 under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
Global AI capex chart: USD 60bn in 2022, USD 488bn in 2025, and UBS estimates of USD 1trn in 2026 and USD 1.4trn in 2027.
vol_and_positioning: Index-level implied volatility is relatively subdued, which lowers option costs for capital preservation structures.
Single-stock volatility is elevated, raising option premiums that structured yield strategies can monetize.
Cboe S&P 500 Dispersion Index has risen, which supports stock selection and low-net or market-neutral hedge fund strategies.
The 10 largest companies are about 40% of the S&P 500, so revisions to a few earnings forecasts have an outsized effect on index returns.
Currency volatility is low, which supports carry strategies.
Recommended structures: capital preservation notes, structured yield notes with conditional coupons, and predefined-entry strategies with staggered maturities and entry levels.
geopolitical: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil up 52% year to date and surged refined-product prices.
Difficult negotiations between Washington and Tehran make a Middle East settlement unlikely near term, with further US escalation a risk.
The war in Ukraine is expected to continue into 2027, supporting European defense spending and limiting additional Russian energy supply.
US-China competition persists across technology, semiconductors, critical minerals and AI infrastructure, with a possible further tightening of export controls.
The EU's measures targeting Chinese EVs and wider Europe-China trade tensions.
Asian economies face growing pressure to choose sides as technology ecosystems split into competing blocs.
US regulations on remote access to advanced chips could slow data-center capex into 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects AI capex to reach USD 1.6tr in 2027. Hyperscaler cloud revenue grew 57% y/y in 3Q26, contracted orders total USD 2.5tr, and token usage is up sixfold as costs more than halved.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex could outrun returns through slower cloud growth, weaker enterprise deployment, falling AI pricing power, circular financing, and power and permitting constraints.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capacity expansion outstripping demand growth, a meaningful slowdown in AI lab revenue growth, weaker cloud utilization, or falling AI costs failing to stimulate enough new usage.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation reflects one-off shocks, services inflation has fallen from 7.3% to 3.1%, and AI could boost productivity and be disinflationary.
tension_points.bear_case: Defense, AI and energy-security investment plus larger fiscal deficits push real rates structurally higher, and resilient but less efficient supply chains add cost.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wage growth reaccelerating, second-round effects from supply shocks, or central banks showing less willingness to return inflation to target.

tension_points.bull_case: No fixed debt threshold triggers a crisis. If nominal growth exceeds funding costs, debt ratios stabilize, and policymakers retain tools such as buybacks and domestic-ownership incentives.
tension_points.bear_case: Refinancing at higher yields, withdrawal of central bank support and heavy private financing needs could force an abrupt market adjustment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bond auctions becoming difficult to cover, signs fiscal authorities cannot stabilize debt, or sovereign stress spreading to banks and credit markets.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets have repeatedly absorbed shocks, supply chains and energy markets have adapted, and diplomacy could stabilize energy.
tension_points.bear_case: Disruption to Russian or Middle East energy, or escalating US-China restrictions on semiconductors, AI infrastructure and rare earths, could cause lasting economic damage.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained disruption to Middle Eastern shipping or Gulf infrastructure, material loss of energy supplies from the Ukraine war, or changes in Western support altering the military balance.

tension_points.bull_case: Upward capex revisions and a shortening hardware payback period drive another year of earnings growth and pricing gains in North Asian memory and foundry.
tension_points.bear_case: A 2022-style downturn where double ordering unwinds, mainland China adds memory capacity, algorithmic breakthroughs cut compute needs, and memory prices fall from mid-2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slowing AI lab revenue growth, weaker cloud utilization, or falling AI costs failing to generate enough incremental demand to absorb capacity.

theme_stances.theme: US and global equities to neutral
theme_stances.key_argument: High expectations and index concentration make the market more sensitive to earnings disappointment or higher discount rates.
theme_stances.evidence: We have moved global equities to Neutral.

theme_stances.key_argument: Eurozone EPS growth of 15% matches the US from a lower starting valuation and with less dependence on AI-linked companies.
theme_stances.evidence: The Eurozone is our preferred regional equity market.

theme_stances.key_argument: Central bank buying and fiscal worries support gold, while grid and AI demand against slow mine supply supports copper.
theme_stances.evidence: Copper is our preferred industrial metal.
